passages.text: For example, Adam, who came into being according to his likeness, is created blind, is handed down as possessing no knowledge of good or evil, is found to be a transgressor, is expelled from Paradise, and is punished with death. Likewise, the one who formed him, since he does not see from every direction, says at the destruction of Sodom, “Come, and after going down let us see whether they are carrying matters through in accordance with their outcry that is coming to me; but if not, so that I may know,” and thereby shows himself to be ignorant. As for his saying about Adam, “Let us cast him out, lest perhaps, after stretching out his hand, he touch the tree of life and eat, and he will live forever”—his saying “lest perhaps” indicates ignorance, while his addition, “lest perhaps, after eating, he live forever,” also indicates envy. That it is written, “God considered that he had made the human being,” means that he both changes his mind and is ignorant. For “considered” is a reflection by which someone, through ignorance, wishes to determine precisely the outcome of what he intends, or the reflection of someone regretting something that did not turn out according to his intention. That it is written, “And the Lord smelled an odor of fragrance,” belongs to one who is needy, while taking pleasure in the fatty smoke of flesh belongs to one who is not good. Testing—as it is written, “And the Lord tested Abraham”—belongs to one who is evil and ignorant of the outcome of the endurance.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: γνῶσιν ἀγαθοῦ ἢ κακοῦ οὐκ ἔχων παραδέδοται
lexical_decisions.chosen: is handed down as possessing no knowledge of good or evil
lexical_decisions.rationale: The perfect passive παραδέδοται can describe how Adam is transmitted or represented in the received account; “is delivered over while possessing no knowledge” is possible but less coherent in this sequence.

lexical_decisions.chosen: since he does not see from every direction
lexical_decisions.rationale: The literal spatial image of πανταχόθεν is retained rather than replaced with the interpretive abstraction “is not omniscient.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰ κατὰ τὴν κραυγὴν αὐτῶν τὴν ἐρχομένην πρὸς μὲ συντελοῦνται
lexical_decisions.chosen: whether they are carrying matters through in accordance with their outcry that is coming to me
lexical_decisions.rationale: The main text takes συντελοῦνται in an action-oriented middle sense, referring contextually to conduct carried through in correspondence with the outcry; “matters” clarifies the implied object but is not expressed in Greek. A materially different passive reading is possible: “whether they are being brought to an end in accordance with their outcry that is coming to me.”

When Simon isolates μήπως, he treats its expression of apprehension or uncertainty as evidence of ignorance. The word can be represented contextually by “lest,” while “perhaps” makes explicit the uncertainty on which his argument depends.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸ δὲ ἐπαγαγεῖν „μήπως φαγὼν ζήσεται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα“ καὶ φθονεῖ
lexical_decisions.chosen: while his addition, “lest perhaps, after eating, he live forever,” also indicates envy
lexical_decisions.rationale: In the repeated clause μήπως retains its apprehensive and preventive force, connecting Adam’s possible eating and living forever with the accusation of envy; rendering it merely “perhaps” would obscure that connection.

lexical_decisions.chosen: he both changes his mind and is ignorant
lexical_decisions.rationale: Here μετανοεῖ denotes alleged divine reconsideration or regret, not moral-spiritual reorientation toward God.
κνίση is the steam, smoke, or savor produced by burning fat or flesh; the rendering retains the polemically physical image.
τέλος can denote either the outcome or the limit of endurance; “outcome” best fits the claim that testing seeks information about the eventual result.

source_issues.issue: The printed grave accent on μὲ is an apparent accentuation irregularity. The context clearly calls for the first-person pronoun “me,” so the wording remains translatable without supplying missing content.
